piece_type: Instagram post by paid celebrity influencer (video + text)

cases.heading: False or Misleading Risk Presentation
cases.claim: “So, I have an infant and a toddler both who have severe food allergies . . . . Auvi-Q is the only epinephrine autoinjector out there for infants and toddlers.” (AVO) | “AUVI-q® (epinephrine injection, USP) is for life-threatening allergic emergencies.” (SUPER) | “AUVI-q 0.1 mg is for infants and toddlers 16.5-33 lbs.” (text)
cases.context: Post entirely omits risk information; 'For Important Safety Information, visit @auviq_ISI' does not mitigate.
cases.rationale: Efficacy claims with no risk information create misleading impression of safety.
cases.check: Rule: any piece with product name + benefit/use claim must contain risk information in the piece itself; a link/handle to ISI alone fails.
